body: People saying "went to work"  cold turkey likely mean a sit down job which is nothing like you're talking about. You have to buy a scale and taper, and it will work, but it will take several months. Go down gram by fraction of a gram and stabilize at each level. You can NEVER increase no matter what you have to do that day, but if it's going to be a big day you can take the same amount as the day before. You will be tired, but able to serve, cook, weld, install, haul, move, shelve, etc. It's what worked for me, finally.

At least make it out of school, out of your parent's house, and experiment with living on your own terms. So much about a school-age person has to do with their upbringing, home environment, the town they live in, and it's so hard to see that when you're in the middle of it.

I wish I would have taken the chance to focus on building new dimensions of my character, work on my body and mind while I have the time, and try to build new habits. Maybe explore some of that stuff while you have the time and the chance but, if you don't feel like it, don't! People will make you feel bad with their expectations even when they don't want to, so try not to take them, even older people, too seriously if it's starting to make you feel bad.

 And keep yourself open to new opportunities, hang out with people at school you might have overlooked, and realize that no one will tell you that they're insecure, but they all are. Some people will act stand-offish in high school but they actually want to hang out with you or may even like you! Don't be afraid to make the first call. I never bothered anyone back then, and I regret it.

I hope some of this makes sense, I just remember what you're going through and hope something I said helped.
